failure_reason: all three attempts terminated with terminal_reason watchdog_timeout and NaN ground-truth goal distance and clearance. watchdog_timeout is an operational classification, so no scientific outcome was produced or discarded. Each attempt ran a real rollout: the policy verified its identity, passed calibration, and reached tick 200 or beyond before the command watchdog fired
root_cause: not fully determined. watchdog_timeout is a known intermittent operational failure across this batch: 22 of 542 terminal records, about 4 percent, distributed across blocks rather than trending upward (0, 6, 9, 0, 3, 4 per 100 records). Three consecutive occurrences on one identity is far less likely than that base rate alone predicts, so an identity-specific contribution cannot be ruled out. Two candidates were examined and rejected: the SIGSEGV exits at teardown are normal here (neighbouring episodes with four segfaults each completed with accepted scientific outcomes), and memory, GPU and /dev/shm were all clear. One real resource leak was found and cleared: 6,116 stale /tmp/launch_params_* files left behind by ros2 launch, one per node per episode
resolution: the stale /tmp/launch_params_* files were removed, and the identity is released for a fourth attempt. If it fails again the batch will pause again on the same identity, which distinguishes an identity-specific defect from the background intermittent rate. No scientific input was altered and the retry ceiling was not raised
changed: removed stale /tmp/launch_params_* files (infrastructure debris, not evidence)
scripts/run_live_sim_development_episode.sh: remove this episode's launch parameter files during teardown
note: cause not conclusively identified; this is recorded honestly rather than attributed to the leak that was cleaned at the same time
